1.explanation:
• Tile/Tile.mdx & Tile/docs/overview.mdx describe the base <Tile> component and its variants (including <RadioTile>), showing how the underlying <input> is rendered and styled.
• TileGroup/TileGroup.mdx & TileGroup/docs/overview.mdx cover grouping behavior and how required validation can be applied to a group of tiles.
• Form/Form.mdx & Form/docs/overview.mdx explain native HTML form validation, how the browser positions validation bubbles relative to inputs, and how required attributes propagate.  
Together, these documents provide the markup, CSS classes (e.g. .bx--tile-input, .bx--tile-group), and usage patterns needed to reproduce the issue and experiment with repositioning the invisible radio input to fix the validation message placement.
1.bug_scenario: Both screenshots show a <TileGroup> of three <RadioTile> options inside a native HTML <Form> with no option selected at submit. Because the underlying <input type="radio"> is invisible and placed at the top-left of the first tile by default, the browser’s validation “Please select one of these options.” bubble appears in that corner. In light (first image) and dark (second image) themes the error message is pinned to the wrong spot. Ideally, the invisible radio input should be centered at the bottom of the tile or group so the validation bubble appears in a more logical location under the tiles.
